abstract: Accurate protein complex structure modeling requires knowledge of complex stoichiometry, yet the copy numbers of individual subunits are often unknown. Consequently, predicting protein complex stoichiometry has emerged as a major challenge in recent years. Here, we present StoiAgent, a large language model (LLM)-powered AI agent that automates the retrieval and integration of sequence, structural, and literature evidence to predict stoichiometry while preserving interpretable reasoning traces (chain of thoughts) of its evidence assessment and ranking decision. An open-weight LLM model, Qwen3.6-27B, is used by StoiAgent as the LLM backbone to combine sequences, structural templates, AlphaFold3 structure predictions, and literature evidence, and perform stoichiometry candidate generation and ranking. On 56 CASP17 protein complex targets, it achieves top-1 accuracy of 75.0%, which represents a 23.2 percentage-point improvement over PreStoi with AlphaFold3 ranking (51.8%) and matches the top-1 accuracy of StoPred. Moreover, StoiAgent has a higher top-3 and top-5 accuracy than StoPred (85.7% versus 80.4% and 87.5% versus 85.7%, respectively). Furthermore, it outperforms general-purpose frontier LLMs, including ChatGPT and Gemini, in stoichiometry prediction. Case studies further illustrate how StoiAgent evaluates competing assembly hypotheses by integrating complementary evidence, with recorded reasoning traces documenting its decision-making process. Overall, StoiAgent demonstrates the potential of LLM-powered AI agents to improve protein complex stoichiometry prediction through the automated integration of diverse sources of evidence while providing interpretable explanations to guide downstream structure modeling.
